cover.class: Bright white/cyan material: probable cloud, with snow/ice an unresolved alternative; medium confidence in interpretation, low confidence in percentage
Gray-blue textured areas: visible surface or shaded material of unresolved land-cover type; high confidence in appearance, low confidence in identity and percentage
Dark blue-gray bands: probable shadows or shaded boundaries; medium confidence in interpretation, low confidence in percentage

global.landscape: Medium confidence: a strongly heterogeneous scene with extensive bright material and darker textured areas. Cloud obscuration is plausible and provisionally favored, but snow/ice and terrain shading cannot be excluded. Low confidence: the underlying landscape type is indeterminate.
global.season_cues: High confidence: neither rendering shows a strong vegetation signal. Low confidence: this could reflect obscuration, sparse vegetation, or a snow-covered season; no specific season or phenological stage is defensible.
global.heterogeneity: High confidence: strong brightness contrasts occur over tens to hundreds of meters, with irregular bright patches, granular gray areas, and narrow dark margins. Medium confidence: obscuration and shading contribute substantially to the apparent heterogeneity.

spectral.true_color: High confidence: the image is dominated by nearly saturated white, pale cyan, mottled gray-blue, and dark blue-gray. Bright regions have little visible internal detail, while darker regions show coarse granular texture. Green and brown tones are weak or absent.
spectral.false_color: High confidence: the same bright and dark structures persist. Cyan fringes are conspicuous, and gray areas have muted bluish or slightly purplish tones. There are no extensive bright-red patches indicating an unambiguous strong near-infrared vegetation response.

implications.claim: The renderings do not provide a clear signal of vigorous exposed vegetation; obscuration prevents interpreting this as vegetation absence.
Bright lobate patches with adjacent dark margins are consistent with clouds and shadows, although snow/ice remains a credible alternative.
Cyan coloration alone cannot establish surface wetness or distinguish cloud, snow, ice, and display effects.
No water body is securely identified, so water turbidity and flooding cannot be assessed.
Gray textured areas could include rock, sparse vegetation, built surfaces, or shaded snow/ice; their color does not securely distinguish these classes.
Bare-soil exposure, soil moisture, and built-surface abundance cannot be estimated reliably from these renderings.

spectral.not_revealed: High confidence: these display images do not provide calibrated reflectance, quantitative vegetation indices, cloud height, snow depth, surface temperature, soil moisture, water depth, or reliable material composition. They also cannot establish temporal change, crop identity, or management history.

interpretation.claim: Cloud obscuration and associated shadows are the provisional explanation for much of the scene's brightness pattern.
interpretation.evidence: Levels 2–4; top_left, top_center, middle_right, and bottom_center: bright lobes, cyan fringes, and repeated adjacent dark bands.

interpretation.claim: Snow/ice with shaded or exposed rough terrain remains an alternative scene interpretation.
interpretation.evidence: Levels 1–4; all cells: extensive white/cyan material, gray rough areas, and weak red response are compatible with this alternative but are not diagnostic.

interpretation.claim: Agricultural land use, crop types, crop rotation, and field management cannot be established.
interpretation.evidence: Levels 2–3; middle_left, middle_center, and bottom_center: no securely identifiable field boundaries, crop rows, or irrigation structures.

interpretation.claim: Forestry and settlement cannot be distinguished confidently within the gray textured areas.
interpretation.evidence: Levels 2–4; top_left, middle_center, and bottom_right: granular texture without resolved tree crowns, building footprints, or a convincing road network.

interpretation.claim: Vegetation vigor and ecological condition remain indeterminate.
interpretation.evidence: Level 4; all cells: little conspicuous red in false color, combined with extensive bright material and shading.

interpretation.claim: Irrigation, harvest, erosion, flooding, and clearing are not demonstrable.
interpretation.evidence: Levels 2–4; all cells: no securely identified process-specific morphology and no temporal comparison.

interpretation.claim: A biome or climate setting cannot be assigned reliably.
interpretation.evidence: Levels 1 and 4; all cells: cloud versus snow/ice ambiguity and unresolved underlying land cover. Even confirmed snow would not uniquely identify climate or biome.

High confidence: scene-edge truncation makes the full size and connectivity of several bright features unknown.
High confidence: a single acquisition cannot establish change, seasonality, management history, or active surface processes.

summaries.w25: Bright patches and gray textured areas dominate. Cloud/shadow interpretation has medium confidence; snow/ice remains possible. Underlying land cover and vegetation condition are unresolved.
summaries.w50: The patch contains bright white/cyan material, gray textured areas, and dark boundary bands. Clouds and shadows are provisionally favored with medium confidence; snow/ice remains possible. No strong red vegetation response is visible with high confidence. Land use, ecological condition, season, and climate cannot be reliably assigned.
summaries.w100: Bright white/cyan material occupies approximately 46%, gray textured areas 45%, and dark bands 9%, with low confidence in these visual estimates. Clouds and shadows are provisionally favored with medium confidence because bright lobes repeatedly adjoin dark margins, especially at top left and bottom center. Snow/ice remains an unresolved alternative. High confidence: false color shows no extensive bright-red vegetation response, but obscuration prevents conclusions about vegetation absence or health. High confidence: roads, fields, buildings, and water bodies are not securely identified, leaving land use, ecological state, active processes, biome, and climate unresolved.
summaries.w200:
The 1.2 km patch is strongly heterogeneous, with high confidence in its visible pattern but limited confidence in physical interpretation. Estimated apparent cover is 46% bright white/cyan material, 45% gray textured areas, and 9% dark bands; these percentages have low confidence and do not describe validated ground cover.

Clouds and associated shadows are provisionally favored with medium confidence. Bright lobes and neighboring dark margins recur at top left, upper center/right, middle right, and bottom center. Snow/ice and terrain shading remain an alternative with low confidence. The central gray area is granular, while bright interiors are comparatively smooth and nearly saturated, with high confidence in those observations.

High confidence: false color contains no extensive strong red response. This limits evidence for vigorous exposed vegetation but cannot establish vegetation absence, dormancy, or stress. High confidence: no convincing field system, road network, settlement, or water body is resolved. Consequently, crop identity, forestry, irrigation, harvest, flooding, erosion, ecological condition, and climate remain indeterminate. High confidence: native 10 m sampling, display enlargement, bright-area saturation, and uncertain obscuration restrict object identification and feature measurements.
summaries.w400:
The scene contains extensive bright white/cyan patches interspersed with gray-blue textured areas and dark boundary bands. High confidence applies to this visual description. Low-confidence area estimates assign 46% to bright material, 45% to gray textured areas, and 9% to dark bands. These are apparent image classes, not a reliable inventory of underlying land cover.

Cloud obscuration and associated shadows are provisionally favored with medium confidence. At top left, a bright patch borders a curved dark band. A larger bright complex extends through the upper center and right. Middle left contains interlocking bright and gray lobes, while middle center contains a broad granular gray region. Bottom center has a conspicuous white patch with a cyan fringe and dark lower margin. These spatial observations have high confidence. Snow/ice adjoining shaded or exposed terrain remains an alternative physical interpretation with low confidence.

The major bright groupings span roughly 100–650 m, with low confidence in their dimensions and separation. High confidence: boundaries are irregular and often lobate, and no convincing field system, road network, individual building, or water body is identifiable. Dark bands could include cast shadows or terrain shading, with medium confidence in that ambiguity.

High confidence: both renderings retain similar bright and dark structures, and false color shows no extensive bright-red vegetation response. This supports only the absence of a clear exposed vigorous-vegetation signal. It does not establish vegetation absence, poor health, or dormancy. High confidence: moisture, water turbidity, bare-soil abundance, and built-surface abundance cannot be assessed securely.

High confidence: crop types, rotation, forestry, settlement, irrigation, harvest, clearing, erosion, flooding, ecological condition, biome, and climate are unresolved. The principal limitations are uncertain cloud versus snow/ice identity, native 10 m sampling, edge-truncated features, and bright-area loss of detail. Medium confidence: display stretching and interpolation may accentuate cyan fringes. High confidence: a single pair of rendered band combinations cannot establish temporal change or quantitative surface properties.
